statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score; the last observed path, Friday's new 31,017.53 intraday record fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 range with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, is orderly two-way discovery rather than the extension pattern Tail measures. Stress is 71 in the high band because a record U.S. diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel emergency release, an unconfirmed Houthi claim of a missile and drone strike on an Aramco facility in Riyadh and a 10-year that reversed higher to 5.2939% on weak payrolls all remain unresolved with no venue able to price them. Confidence is 84 on independently re-verified session levels, yields, energy prices and a verified seven-day calendar, offset by the absence of any live price path.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band for all 24 scored hours, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON and green throughout. Twenty-three of those hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt; the restart at 22:00Z on 4 October falls at the start of the final scored hour, so that slot conditionally contains the week's first Nasdaq-100 price discovery and carries the window's highest Tail at 16. The Gulf cash session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October is the only live venue with direct exposure to the claimed Riyadh refinery strike; under the inherited delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure or the current action. A narrow danger window is published for the restart hour as a dated discontinuity checkpoint; it does not change the Tail-derived mapping. The next scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October, with FOMC minutes on 7 October.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while a record diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel release and an unconfirmed Riyadh refinery strike keep Stress at 71 into a 22:00Z Sunday restart
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels are independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is that the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 and at the bottom of a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt.

The session's driver was the September employment report, taken here from the primary release: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, the unemployment rate was 4.2%, and average hourly earnings edged up 0.1% to $37.81 for a 3.0% annual rate. Equities read that as cementing a Fed hold at the 28 October meeting, but the curve did not follow: the 10-year traded as low as 5.17% immediately after the data before reversing to 5.2939%, about 6 basis points higher on the day, and the 2-year ended at 4.8414%, about 5 basis points higher. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so Friday's move extended an already elevated curve. A record equity close against rising long yields on weak labour data is a legitimate Stress and Confidence input; on this contract it is not a Tail input.

The energy complex is the dominant Stress driver. The G7 and its partners agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and refined products over four months, coordinated through the IEA, with a frontloaded substantial diesel release inside the first 20 days, after the U.S. national average diesel price reached a record $6.52 per gallon on 22 September and stood at $6.37 on Friday. Brent briefly fell below $100 on the announcement before recovering to about $102.25, and WTI reached a one-month low near $88 before trimming losses to roughly $91. Cited expert views hold that the release will press prices lower only briefly because underlying supply remains below normal. The OPEC+ participating countries also meet online on 4 October to review November targets, which are widely expected to be left unchanged; because the exact hour is not reliably published it is carried as a driver checkpoint rather than as a dated calendar event.

Against that offset sits the escalation thread. A large plume of smoke and fire was reported in the vicinity of an Aramco facility in Riyadh on Saturday, and the Houthi military spokesman later said the site had been targeted with ballistic missiles and drones in retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sanaa and other Yemeni provinces, which he put at 94 in 24 hours. Saudi authorities have not confirmed an attack and Aramco has not commented; damage, casualties and any throughput or export effect remain unconfirmed, and separate weekend reports of tanker incidents near the Strait of Hormuz could not be verified for this publication and are therefore not scored. None of this is scoreable as a Nasdaq-100 price path while every relevant venue is closed, and on this contract event importance and geopolitical discontinuity raise Stress and shape Confidence until observed market structure supports Tail.

What changes in this publication is the window itself. The CME equity-index restart at 22:00Z on 4 October now falls at the start of the final scored hour rather than beyond the window, so the last forecast slot conditionally contains the first Nasdaq-100 price discovery of the week. Tail rises along the approach from 3 to 11 and reaches 16 in the restart hour, remaining in the low band throughout because gap and thin-liquidity risk is a discontinuity rather than observed mean-reversion failure, and because no reopening level, gap direction or retracement behaviour has been observed. A shallow or failed first retracement after the restart would be the earliest genuine Tail evidence; an orderly two-way auction would validate the low-band reading carried through the halt. The week ahead is moderate on U.S. macro: ISM Services on Monday, the trade balance, a Bowman speech and a 3-year auction on Tuesday, FOMC minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims and a 30-year auction on Thursday and preliminary Michigan sentiment on Friday, with the next rate decision not until 28 October. The shared Finviz context was not usable for this run: it was collected on 29 September, roughly four days old against the 90-minute freshness bound, and is marked partial, so the assessment rests entirely on independent research and the evidence failed open as the contract requires.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The window opens at 23:00Z on 2 October with Tail 11 and Stress 71 under a mixed mode, then decays as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 11 to 3 by 12:00Z on 3 October and the mode settles to normal from 00:00Z onward. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z and then climbs steadily back to 70 by 22:00Z as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and finally produced a claimed strike on a Riyadh refinery. Confidence held in a narrow 81 to 88 range throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path. No hour required an unavailable slot and no historical opinion was revised.
outlookSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them. Tail is held at 3 through 11:00Z on 4 October, then rises along the restart approach to 11 by 21:00Z and to 16 in the 22:00Z slot that conditionally contains the reopening auction, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 71 to a peak of 79 and remains in the high band, because a record diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel release, an unconfirmed Riyadh refinery strike and a 10-year that reversed higher to 5.2939% accumulate with no venue able to price them. Confidence eases from 84 to a low of 77 before the restart as Friday's levels age, lifting modestly during the Gulf cash session and recovering to 82 once live prices return. A narrow danger window marks the restart hour as a dated discontinuity checkpoint.
